sections.COMMENTS:
The Eastern Southern Alps are the eastern portion of the late Cretaceous-Quaternary S-verging back-thrust belt of the Alpine chain, bounded to the north by the Insubric-Periadriatic line (Doglioni and Bosellini, 1987; Castellarin and Cantelli, 2000). The outer thrust front is composed by NE-SW to E-W trending faults and folds emerging along the mountain front or buried below the Quaternary foredeep and continental sediments of the Veneto-Friuli plain (Galadini et al., 2005), which were used to define the Neogene-Quaternary timing of activity of these structures (Caputo et al., 2010). To the east the Southalpine thrusts interact with the NW-SE trending, dextral strike-slip faults of the Idrija fault system in the Slovenia border region (Bajc et al., 2001; Burrato et al., 2008; Kastelic et al., 2008). Similar structural setting can be deduced for the more northern parts of the South Alpine unit, where the south vergent thrusts of the Friulain Alps and Pre-alps interact with the strike-slip extrusion structure of the Periadriatic fault system.
This Source represents the seismogenic portion of the W-E oriented Fella active fault located in the Val Canale. The minimum and maximum depth were inferred from geologic and regional structural setting (Poli et al., 2002; Ponton, 2010; Reinecker and Lenhardt, 1999). The strike is based on geologic and geomorphological maps and data (Nussbaum, 2000; Burrato et al., 2008; Ponton, 2010), while the dip of the source was inferred from geological and geomorphological observations. The rake was inferred from regional structural and earthquake data (focal mechanisms and horizontal maximum stress orientations combined with the geometry of the source) from Reinecker and Lenhardt (1999). The slip rate was inferred considering finite element modeling and geodynamic considerations from Kastelic and Carafa, 2012 together with available geodetic data (Devoti et al., 2002).

pictures.c: Figure 1: Structural setting of the Southern Alps in the area of NE Italy and W Slovenia (Burrato et al., 2008). The Tarvisio seismogenic source is marked by the letter FE.

pictures.t: Geological profile across the southern Alps of northeastern Friuli
pictures.c: Figure 3: N-S oriented profile through the Friulian plane and the Southern Alps (NE Italy) showing the prevailing south vergent thrust structure; the Tarvisio seismogenic source in the DISS model is identified as the southern-most fault of the Periadriatic fault zone that is an alternative interpretation  to the south dipping fault shown in this profile (Ponton, 2010).

pictures.t: Geological profile across the southern Alps of northwestern Friuli
pictures.c: Figure 3: N-S oriented profile through the Friulian plane and the Southern Alps (Poli et al., 2002). The Tarvisio seismogenic source corresponds to the leading plane of the north dipping northern most fault zone shown in the profile.
Figure 3: Orientation of the main compressional stress axis for the Alpine area (Reinecker and Lenhardt, 1999).

Figure 3: Focal mechanism solutions for the registered earthquakes in the Alpine region (Reinecker and Lenhardt, 1999). The dextral-strike slip solutions in the area of the Tarvisio correspond to the rake of the seismogenic source.
